title.narrative: Enhancing Access to Essential WASH Items and Hygiene Promotion for Cholera Outbreak-Affected Population in Al-Hol camp in North East Syria

description.narrative: ltpgtAs of October 2023, approximately 13.56 million individuals, including 44% children, are in urgent need of WASH support, reflecting an increase of approximately 2.6% since 2022. The protracted crisis, lack of routine maintenance, shortage of experienced staff, drought and scarce water resources combined with absence of integrated water resources management, drastic reduction of budget allocations and inflation, continue to contribute to the reduction of access to basic WASH services. This situation has been further aggravated by the earthquakes in February 2023 and the transitional phase in Syria that commenced on December 8, 2024, underscoring the critical demand for basic WASH services.ltbrgtIn particular, the displaced people in Al-Hol camp in Northeastern Syria faces an urgent need for immediate interventions to prevent the spread of epidemic diseases, especially in an environment marked by extreme overcrowding and insufficient basic services. Al-Hol camp, which accommodates around 40,000 displaced individuals and refugees, mostly women and children, is one of the largest displacement sites in the region. The health risks in this context are heightened by limited access to clean water and safe sanitation facilities, creating a fertile environment for diseases such as cholera, which has intensified in Syria since 2022 due to deteriorating infrastructure and living conditions.ltbrgtIn response to these challenging humanitarian circumstances, EPDC is planning to implement a project aimed at distributing cholera prevention kits and conducting intensive awareness campaigns. This initiative seeks to address the health crisis through an integrated approach that combines emergency relief with long-term preventive measures, thereby protecting the most vulnerable communities and enhancing their resilience against epidemics.ltbrgtThe project has two main components. The first involves the distribution of 5190 kit over 3 rounds (1,730 kit per month)cholera prevention kits, accompanied with conducting awareness sessions and hygiene/cholera brochures designed in accessible language with colorful educational imagery, targeting approximately 8,650 individuals across 1,730 households in three distribution rounds within Al-Hol camp. The second component focuses on conducting intensive awareness campaigns, and interactive educational theater, targeting around 11,500 individual directly. These campaigns will target children and include the distribution of posters in gathering areas, conveying clear messages regarding handwashing, water sterilization, early recognition of cholera symptoms, and dispelling myths that may hinder timely treatment. Local teams will receive prior training to ensure effective engagement with the community's cultural context and to achieve the project's objectives.ltbrgtThe success of this initiative relies not only on material resources but also on meaningful community participation in the design and implementation of the campaigns. By involving community leaders and women activists in the awareness teams, the credibility and impact of the messages are significantly enhanced. Separate sessions will be organized for women, who predominantly serve as caregivers, to equip them with practical skills such as preparing homemade oral rehydration solutions. Children will be engaged through educational activities, including songs and drawings, to promote awareness. This participatory approach not only enhances the effectiveness of the interventions but also fosters a sense of collective responsibility for public health within the community.lt/pgtltpgtIf implemented efficiently, the project could reduce cholera cases by up to 70% within six months. Challenges include logistical difficulties and resistance from traditional practices. The project relies on local partnerships and coordination with health authorities for rapid treatment and integrates with infrastructure improvements to boost long-term prevention.ltbrgtlt/pgt
